note: The only place platform names appear in the reader. Every entry is unverified (verified_at null) until a manual live check and a human review; an unverified route that fails simply falls through to the next rung. hosts: exact names or '*.suffix'. path: a regular expression on the URL path; its named groups become template variables, and query parameters are available as {q_<name>}. path_by_host: a different path pattern for some of the hosts (such as a short-link host). Other template variables: {scheme} {host} {port_suffix} {path} {query} {url_enc}, and {key} for a user key read from the environment variable named in 'env' (always REMORSEARCH_*; 'env_aliases' lists older names that are still accepted; the value is never stored or logged). A key named in this packaged table is sent only to the hosts this table names for it, and only REMORSEARCH_* variables and the aliases listed here are ever read, whatever route table a run uses. official: kind 'feed' (scope 'item' keeps only the entry that links to the page; scope 'all' keeps every entry, such as a thread or review feed), 'oembed', or 'api' (read only by the provider adapter named in 'adapter', uxresearch/<adapter>.py, which has its own fields: the youtube adapter reads id_from, id_pattern, url, comments_url, page_size, max_pages, quota_units_per_call, quota_reset_tz, retention_days and policy_note; an 'api' route with no adapter is skipped). alternates: the site's own mobile or AMP twins. author_from: subdomain | path_segment | page. profile_paths: first path segments that name a person's channel or profile on the platform's hosts; the privacy scrubber replaces such URLs. login_hosts: a redirect there is an auth_gate stop. Four scope lists are checked before any request, on every redirect hop, route and alternate, in this order: the researcher's deny list, search_pages (refused at the start with exit 2; a stop when reached by a redirect), the never_call endpoints of discovery entries switched off (the same), out_of_scope (private channels), then terms_restricted. A terms_restricted entry comes only from a published or reported restriction with its sources, never from a guess: status 'confirmed' when the clause itself was read (never lifted), 'reported' when only secondary sources report it (lifted for a run only by the user's own terms check in the brief, access_policy.terms_checked, whose result is permits_this_reading; a lifted host then has a budget of 10 documents). official_route names the platform whose official route may still run for such a host (official-only mode: no page request, no render capture). Host names cover their subdomains in every list. The packaged scope lists always apply, also when a run uses another route table (--routes), which can add entries but never remove them. Verify every note live before relying on it.

official.policy_note: YouTube API data: keep it at most 30 days (retention_until), then delete it or read it again; never profile commenters, and never record age, race, religion, political leaning, sexual orientation, health or another protected-attribute cue against an author key (use such cues in segment-level claims only).
